sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Brentford host Everton at Brentford Community Stadium with both sides level on 46 points (7th vs 8th). Brentford are winless in 4 but unbeaten, while Everton arrive with 3 wins in their last 5. The last 2 head-to-heads saw a Brentford win at Goodison (4-2) and a 1-1 draw here.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Brentford have drawn 4 straight (0-0 at Leeds, 2-2 vs Wolves, 2-2 at West Ham, 0-0 at Bournemouth), showing improved defensive control but mixed chance conversion. Everton’s last 5: wins vs Chelsea (3-0), Burnley (2-0) and at Newcastle (3-2), plus narrow losses to Manchester United and Arsenal. Everton have 2 clean sheets in that run and are efficient without the ball.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Brentford are unbeaten in 3 vs Everton. The last meeting swung Brentford’s way (xG 0.89-2.66), while the most recent clash here finished 1-1 after a balanced xG (1.48-1.37). Historically, 5 of the last 7 head-to-heads have had fewer goals, though the 4-2 in January was an exception.

sections.subtitle: Season stats and tactical notes
sections.text: Brentford create many high-quality chances (94 big chances, 3rd), break quickly (fast breaks 1st), and are dangerous late (76-90 mins: 15 goals, 31%). They rely on direct play (47% possession, 78.8% pass accuracy) and set-piece power (9 headers). Everton’s profile is tighter (37 scored, 35 conceded), with strength in set pieces and aerial duels through James Tarkowski and Michael Keane, and delivery from James Garner (11 big chances created). Everton also score late (76-90 mins: 12, 20%), so game state swings are likely.

sections.subtitle: Key players
sections.text: Igor Thiago leads Brentford’s attack (19 league goals; 4 in last 5) and was decisive in the 4-2 at Goodison. Dango Ouattara and Kevin Schade add pace on transitions. For Everton, Beto is in form (3 goals, 1 assist in last 5), Garner provides supply, and Tarkowski has consistently performed well in this fixture.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Farai Hallam averages 3.6 yellows and very few reds. Brentford average 1.87 yellows per match, and recent head-to-heads trend to lower card counts. Brentford average 4.8 corners; Everton’s recent totals vary, but set pieces remain a key route, suggesting an average corner count.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: The Sofascore model gives Brentford a slight edge (home 43%, draw 28%, away 29%) with both teams to score at 48%. Expect a tight match where Brentford’s chance creation and late-game threat can tilt it, while Everton’s set pieces keep them competitive. Lean narrowly towards Brentford, with the draw a realistic alternative.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Brentford and Everton are level at half-time (1-1) at Brentford Community Stadium. Igor Thiago converted a penalty on 3 minutes; Beto equalised with a header on 26 minutes from an Idrissa Gueye delivery. The first half was balanced in possession (Brentford 52%), but the home side carried the greater threat in chance quality and output (expected goals 1.26 vs 0.82; shots on target 3 vs 2; big chances 2 vs 1) and hit the woodwork once. Everton were stronger in duels and in the air (aerial duels won 64%), with the back line busy in clearances.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Brentford started aggressively with sustained pressure that led to the early penalty. After a more even spell, Everton enjoyed their best period from around the 20th to early 30th minute, scoring and maintaining pressure soon after. The momentum then swung back, with Brentford finishing the half strongly in a prolonged attacking spell before the interval. Overall, the half moved in distinct phases, with each side enjoying one major period of control.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical patterns and match-ups
halftimeSections.text: Brentford created most when combining quickly into central areas and attacking second balls, rather than relying on aerial contests (their aerial success 36%). Everton threatened through direct entries and wide deliveries to Beto, while Idrissa Gueye and James Garner disrupted build-up and progression (Gueye 1 assist, 1 big chance created; Garner 2 interceptions). Brentford's right side applied pressure (Kevin Schade 2 tackles won; Michael Kayode 2 interceptions), but this can leave space behind the full-backs. Everton's back line dealt with volume into the area effectively (Jarrad Branthwaite 6 clearances; James Tarkowski 5; Vitaliy Mykolenko 5).

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key numbers at half-time
halftimeSections.text: Possession: Brentford 52% vs Everton 48. Expected goals: 1.26 vs 0.82. Shots on target: 3 vs 2. Big chances: 2 vs 1. Final-third entries: 34 vs 33. Penalty-area entries: 17 vs 15. Aerial duels won: 36% vs 64%. Corners: 2 vs 1.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Expect Brentford to emphasise ground combinations, cut-backs and through balls to isolate Igor Thiago between centre-backs, rather than frequent high crosses. Everton are likely to continue targeting early deliveries to Beto and set-pieces, where they hold an aerial advantage. With possessions won high similar for both (2 each) and penalty-area entries close, the next decisive moment in the box is likely to shape the result. If Brentford sustain their late-half tempo and precision, they look marginally more likely to score next; Everton remain a threat whenever they can increase crossing volume or draw set-pieces.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: Referee information not provided. Cards: 1 yellow for Jordan Pickford; no other cautions. Corners: Brentford 2, Everton 1. Outlook: the duel profile suggests a competitive but controlled contest; anticipate 1–2 further bookings if pressing intensity remains. Corner count should rise with Everton's crossing and Brentford's pressure; expect roughly 4–6 more corners.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Brentford to edge a narrow second half, with the home side likelier to score next. Predicted final score: Brentford 2–1 Everton. Most likely next scorer: Igor Thiago, given his involvement and penalty responsibility.
